tasks.title: Dark Stores
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a business class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What aspect of dark stores does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: Their influence on the retail market and society
options.B: Their architectural design and layout
options.C: Their similarities to traditional storefronts
options.D: Their role in the history of warehouse development

questions.stem: According to the talk, why can dark stores offer lower prices?

options.A: Because they sell large quantities of goods
options.B: Because they are not focused on making a profit
options.C: Because they obtain less expensive products
options.D: Because they have lower overhead expenses

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention grocery delivery?

options.A: To illustrate how dark stores compete with traditional supermarkets
options.B: To compare delivery speeds in urban and nonurban environments
options.C: To suggest that dark stores mainly sell perishable items
options.D: To explain why consumers are willing to pay higher fees

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about dark stores and employment?

options.A: Many temporary employees are needed to set dark stores up.
options.B: Employees in dark stores need to be comfortable with technology.
options.C: Dark stores do not need many in-store workers.
options.D: Dark stores are able to pay their employees more.

tasks.title: Poverty Point
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the lecture?

options.A: To describe how trade networks developed among ancient societies in North America
options.B: To highlight an ancient site that required large-scale planning
options.C: To explain the role of metal tools in ancient construction
options.D: To compare different types of prehistoric earthen mounds

questions.stem: What aspect of the earthen mounds is most impressive to the speaker?

options.A: Their extreme height
options.B: Their varying geometric shapes
options.C: The artifacts found inside them
options.D: The knowledge required to build them

questions.stem: What does the speaker emphasize about how the structures at Poverty Point were built?

options.A: They required advanced knowledge of metal technology.
options.B: They depended on materials from distant regions.
options.C: They involved a large amount of manual effort.
options.D: They were completed in a short period of time.

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about the Mississippi River?

options.A: It contained resources that were used for construction.
options.B: It was the main source of food for people at Poverty Point.
options.C: It connected people at Poverty Point to distant areas.
options.D: It enabled people from Poverty Point to relocate to other regions.

tasks.title: Egyptian Mummies
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The differences between Egyptian and Scottish mummies
options.B: The discovery of prehistoric mummies in a surprising location
options.C: The processes that gradually turn mummies into skeletons
options.D: The reasons that Bronze Age people practiced mummification

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about Scotland?

options.A: Its climate is not favorable for typical methods of preserving bodies.
options.B: Its rainy weather makes archaeological research challenging.
options.C: Its oldest skeletons date back to around 4000 B.C.E.
options.D: It may have many Bronze Age sites similar to Cladh Hallan.

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what did radiocarbon dating reveal?

options.A: A pile of bones belonged to two different people.
options.B: A man and a woman had died around 1500 B.C.E.
options.C: Two objects that looked like skeletons were not made of bone.
options.D: Two people were buried long after they had died.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention butter?

options.A: To point out an animal fat frequently used to preserve bodies
options.B: To show that ancient people understood a property of peat bogs
options.C: To help illustrate how swamps break down organic material
options.D: To suggest an ingredient possibly used in a prehistoric burial ritual

tasks.title: LEDs and Incandescent Light
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a physiology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: Research into the health benefits of a modern technology
options.B: The unintended consequences of a technological innovation
options.C: Differences between artificial lighting and natural sunlight
options.D: How different types of light are seen by the human eye

questions.stem: What benefit of LED bulbs does the speaker emphasize?

options.A: Low cost of bulb production
options.B: Low energy use
options.C: Brightness
options.D: Stress reduction for humans

questions.stem: What comparison does the speaker make between the light from incandescent bulbs and the light from LEDs?

options.A: Incandescent bulbs emit less near-infrared light.
options.B: Incandescent bulbs emit light from a broader range of the spectrum.
options.C: LEDs emit a steadier light that is not subject to flickering.
options.D: LEDs emit light that is more similar to natural sunlight.

questions.stem: What is the professor's concern about the advanced LED systems that some experts like?

options.A: They might have negative effects on mood.
options.B: They are unsuitable for use in medical settings.
options.C: Their high cost might prevent their widespread use.
options.D: They produce almost no near-infrared light.

tasks.title: Sleep and Cognitive Function
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The effects of caffeine on sleep
options.B: The different stages of deep sleep
options.C: Common sleep disorders and their treatments
options.D: The benefits of sleep for cognitive function

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about memory consolidation?

options.A: It occurs mainly during deep sleep stages.
options.B: It affects problem-solving abilities.
options.C: It happens primarily in people with sleep disorders.
options.D: It allows the brain to process emotional experiences.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention mood swings?

options.A: To highlight common symptoms of stress
options.B: To point out the impact of sleep deprivation on emotional regulation
options.C: To explain the effects of sleep hygiene on problem-solving abilities
options.D: To illustrate the various stages of sleep

questions.stem: What advice does the speaker give for improving sleep quality?

options.A: Avoid stressful experiences
options.B: Maintain a regular sleep schedule
options.C: Avoid all caffeine consumption
options.D: Spend more time in bed

tasks.title: Keystone Species and Yellowstone Wolves
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a science podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about arches in architecture?

options.A: To point out a similarity to rock arches in nature
options.B: To help illustrate an important concept
options.C: To argue against a common comparison
options.D: To show a difference between life science and technology fields

questions.stem: According to the talk, what is a keystone species?

options.A: A species that is necessary to maintain balance in an ecosystem
options.B: A species that has no predators within an ecosystem
options.C: A species that is too numerous for a healthy ecosystem
options.D: A species that is negatively affected by environmental changes

questions.stem: In the early 20th century, what happened to the wolves in Yellowstone National Park?

options.A: Their population increased dramatically when their prey population increased.
options.B: They became a government-protected species.
options.C: They were eliminated over farming and safety concerns.
options.D: Their population decreased significantly because of disease.

questions.stem: How did an increasing elk population affect the Yellowstone ecosystem?

options.A: Many species were negatively affected due to the elk's diet.
options.B: Various animals that prey on elk were attracted to the area.
options.C: Some areas developed an overgrowth of plants while others had too little vegetation.
options.D: The population and range of the wolves also increased.

tasks.title: Pluto and New Horizons
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on an astronomy podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker discuss the Kuiper Belt at the beginning of the talk?

options.A: To explain why Pluto's status changed
options.B: To illustrate Pluto's size
options.C: To emphasize how far Pluto is from the Sun
options.D: To make a point about Pluto's shape

questions.stem: How did new data change scientists' understanding of Pluto?

options.A: It has a longer orbit than previously thought.
options.B: It has a wider variety of features than previously thought.
options.C: It used to be larger in the past than previously thought.
options.D: It has larger amounts of rainfall than previously thought.

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about convection in Pluto's ice basin?

options.A: It is making the surface of the ice basin grow larger.
options.B: It suggests that volcanoes exist on Pluto.
options.C: It continuously moves warmer ice to the basin's surface.
options.D: It creates strong winds that blow across Pluto's surface.

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what could the presence of an ocean on Pluto mean?

options.A: Pluto orbits closer to the Sun than expected.
options.B: A huge amount of salt exists throughout Pluto.
options.C: Objects in the Kuiper Belt could support life.
options.D: Pluto's ice might be melting.

tasks.title: Lois Mailou Jones
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: How did Lois Mailou Jones' parents support her artistic development?

options.A: By providing the materials she needed
options.B: By paying for her travel to Paris
options.C: By teaching her how to paint
options.D: By taking her to museums

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about Indian Shops?

options.A: It depicts a street scene Jones often saw while studying in Paris.
options.B: It was influenced by Jones' early memories and her studies in Paris.
options.C: It is more geometric than most Impressionist paintings.
options.D: It showed how human-made structures negatively affect nature.

questions.stem: How did Jones' style change later in her career?

options.A: Her artworks became more focused on nature.
options.B: Her artworks began to depict more human-made structures.
options.C: Her artworks began to include a wider variety of colors.
options.D: Her artworks became more abstract.

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about Moon Masque?

options.A: It was more realistic than Jones' earlier work.
options.B: It was one of Jones' last artistic creations.
options.C: It showed Jones' powerful connection to African art.
options.D: It included an object that Jones had brought from Paris.

tasks.title: Stained Glass
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention churches?

options.A: To explain how a traditional technique of making stained glass was developed
options.B: To emphasize the religious significance of stained glass
options.C: To illustrate an effect of stained glass on large spaces
options.D: To point out a use of stained glass that he expects listeners to be familiar with

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention the Arts and Crafts movement?

options.A: To identify the inspiration for Louis Comfort Tiffany's stained glass designs
options.B: To emphasize the natural beauty of stained glass
options.C: To describe the origins of the copper foil technique for making stained glass
options.D: To explain how stained glass became popular in homes

questions.stem: According to the professor, what was a disadvantage of using stained glass in homes?

options.A: It required frequent maintenance.
options.B: It was expensive to produce.
options.C: It resulted in a loss of heat.
options.D: It could break easily during transportation.

questions.stem: What does the speaker indicate about the methods of creating stained glass?

options.A: They have changed greatly over time.
options.B: They tend to yield consistent results.
options.C: They depend on the desired color.
options.D: They often include both lead and copper.

tasks.title: Environmentally Friendly Building Materials
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an architecture class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The renewed use of an old construction material
options.B: Recent advances in sustainable building materials
options.C: The challenges faced by ancient adobe brick builders
options.D: Modern alternatives to adobe bricks

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a new building in Amsterdam?

options.A: It was inspired by adobe construction.
options.B: It is made from very common natural materials.
options.C: It removes carbon from the atmosphere.
options.D: It involves technology that improves insulation.

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about conditions in places in the southwestern United States?

options.A: Major changes in temperature occur there.
options.B: Air there has recently become polluted.
options.C: Not all materials for adobe production are available there.
options.D: More clay for construction is available there than in other places.

questions.stem: What does the speaker emphasize about transportation for construction projects?

options.A: Calculating its costs takes a long time.
options.B: It requires special technology when concrete is used.
options.C: The need for it depends mostly on the location of the project.
options.D: Using adobe bricks helps reduce the need for it.

tasks.title: Solar Power
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a science podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: How does the speaker organize the talk on solar power?

options.A: She outlines solar power's history as an alternative energy resource.
options.B: She lists the technologies involved in generating solar energy.
options.C: She offers case studies of successful solar power projects.
options.D: She compares and contrasts the benefits and challenges of solar power.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention photovoltaic cells?

options.A: To describe how solar panels convert solar energy into electricity
options.B: To discuss innovations in the storage of solar energy
options.C: To explain the cost of installing solar electric systems
options.D: To explain the difficulty and expense of recycling solar panels

questions.stem: Why does the speaker note that all industries produce some carbon dioxide?

options.A: To provide context for a discussion of the solar industry's low carbon footprint
options.B: To suggest that there are reasons for skepticism of the solar industry
options.C: To introduce a discussion about the harmful pollutants given off by solar panels
options.D: To support the claim that solar power provides energy to underserved areas

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is causing a rapid increase in waste from used solar panels?

options.A: Solar panels produced in the last decade cannot be recycled.
options.B: Solar panels in regions with heavy cloud cover are scrapped due to disuse.
options.C: Improvements in panel efficiency are leading to frequent replacement.
options.D: Overuse of solar power is overwhelming panel-recycling systems.

tasks.title: Leonardo da Vinci's Mechanical Knight
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the lecture?

options.A: To review Leonardo da Vinci's most famous artistic works
options.B: To explain how early machines led to modern robotics
options.C: To highlight a lesser-known achievement of Leonardo da Vinci
options.D: To describe technological advances during the Renaissance

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Leonardo's fascination with the human body?

options.A: To indicate his contributions to medical science
options.B: To point out a key influence on Leonardo's designs
options.C: To explain why he spent more time studying anatomy than engineering
options.D: To emphasize Leonardo's artistic skills

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about Leonardo's mechanical understanding?

options.A: It depended on help from other scientists.
options.B: It was shown only in his sketches.
options.C: It was advanced for his time.
options.D: It relied mainly on trial and error.

questions.stem: What attitude does the speaker express toward the reconstruction of "Leonardo's Robot"?

options.A: He is relieved that some design flaws were corrected.
options.B: He is happy that Leonardo's sketches were published.
options.C: He is doubtful of the artistic value of the robot.
options.D: He is impressed by what the robot could do.

tasks.title: Documentary and Ethnographic Films
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a film class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the talk?

options.A: To introduce a new style of documentary
options.B: To outline the process of making a film
options.C: To compare two significant documentaries
options.D: To contrast two kinds of nonfiction films

questions.stem: What attitude does the speaker express when she discusses documentaries?

options.A: She is pleased that documentaries inspire viewers to travel to unfamiliar places.
options.B: She is disappointed that documentaries are becoming less popular.
options.C: She is concerned that viewers are too trusting of documentaries.
options.D: She is frustrated that many documentaries try to tell complicated and confusing stories.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Forest of Bliss?

options.A: To give an example of film with elaborate production
options.B: To give an example of an ethnographic film
options.C: To illustrate the popularity of films about nature
options.D: To illustrate the importance of directors in filmmaking

questions.stem: According to the speaker, how might researchers prepare to make ethnographic films?

options.A: By coming up with a dramatic story they want to tell
options.B: By learning the filming techniques of the culture they are studying
options.C: By spending a long time living within a particular culture
options.D: By analyzing news footage about a particular culture
